description: The line plot illustrates the performance of two methods, “ST-ES” and “Random,” in minimizing the FDE20 metric (minimum final displacement error over 20 predictions) as a function of the number of examples used, ranging from 0 to 8. The x-axis, labeled “Number of Examples,” is linear and spans integer values from 0 to 8 with tick marks at each integer. The y-axis, labeled “minFDE₂₀ (←),” is also linear, ranging from approximately 0.21 to 0.24, with major gridlines and tick labels at 0.21, 0.22, 0.23, and 0.24. The “ST-ES” method is represented by a blue line with circular markers and a solid line style; it starts at approximately 0.24 at 0 examples, drops sharply to about 0.211 at 1 example, and then fluctuates slightly between 0.209 and 0.213 across the remaining examples, ending at approximately 0.213 at 8 examples. The “Random” method is shown as an orange line with circular markers and a solid line style; it begins at approximately 0.23 at 0 examples, dips to about 0.223 at 1 example, then remains relatively stable with minor fluctuations between 0.222 and 0.225 until 6 examples, after which it rises to about 0.228 at 7 examples and 0.23 at 8 examples. A gray rectangular patch is visible near the bottom left of the plot, overlapping the y-axis label, but it does not correspond to any data series or legend entry.
